additional_info.subject: RE: 0379221 - ID0379221-DC/Si-D/DE-[MP / N0 160382401] AC charging socket burned. CRM:00641000658
additional_info.body:
Dear Team,
I hope you are doing well.
As per the reported issue, it appears that the AC socket has been burnt.
We recommend informing the customer not to power on the charger until the Regional Team has conducted an inspection.
The root cause of an AC charging socket burning could be due to several factors, including:
Loose Connections
: If the connections within the socket are loose, it can lead to arcing, which generates excessive heat and can burn the socket over time.
Overloading
: Plugging in devices that draw more current than the socket is rated for can cause overheating, eventually burning the socket.
Faulty Wiring
: Incorrect or old wiring can cause an electrical short, leading to increased resistance, which generates heat and burns the socket.
Corroded Contacts
: Corrosion in the metal contacts of the socket can increase electrical resistance, causing the socket to overheat and burn.
Environmental Factors
: Exposure to moisture or dust can affect the insulation, leading to short circuits and burning.
So, with reference to that check all the Switching devices and contactors which are using for AC charging socket.
Thank you.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Abhinav
